overall: A person who has sat in that school workroom, telling you about a small, real relief, warm and quietly pleased and never selling it. The arc starts with a tired afternoon, settles into plain explanation, lands the time saved low and certain, holds the privacy scene fair and level, and closes softer than the middle.

lines.text: In Mesquite, just east of Dallas, a special education teacher opens one student's folder after the last bell.
lines.intent: Set the scene, an ordinary tired afternoon
lines.note: Unhurried and plain. Weight on 'one student's folder'. Let the last bell settle before moving on.

lines.text: Inside is the start of an IEP, the plan behind that student's special education services. Teachers there reported it took up to three hours. Per student.
lines.intent: Name the problem and its cost
lines.note: Explain the acronym lightly, like a aside to a friend. Land 'three hours' dry, then 'Per student.' short and flat with a full beat after.

lines.text: The district runs fifty two campuses with over thirty six thousand students, so those hours stack up fast.
lines.note: Numbers read matter of fact, no lift. Slight rueful tone on 'stack up fast'.

lines.text: So the district built a tool with Panorama Education. It's called Solara.
lines.note: A gentle lift, the first sign of relief. Say the name Solara simply, a small pause before it.

lines.text: It pulls a student's data from district platforms. Academic data, attendance and behavior pour into one draft.
lines.note: Even and concrete. Light emphasis on 'one draft', the idea of things coming together.

lines.text: From that data, it drafts the student's present levels of achievement.
lines.note: Steady, a little slower. Emphasis on 'drafts'.

lines.text: It can flag a trend, like attendance slipping, or a subject where the child is struggling.
lines.note: Warm and attentive, like noticing something for a kid. Soften slightly on 'struggling'.

lines.text: It was trained on an IEP template, so it lights up the boxes a teacher may have forgotten, instead of making things up.
lines.intent: Reassure that it stays inside the form
lines.note: A small smile in the delivery. Weight on 'instead of making things up', dry.

lines.text: It won't dictate what help a student needs. It doesn't decide eligibility either. Teachers stay the main drivers of the plan.
lines.note: Level and firm, three even beats. Emphasis on 'Teachers' in the last sentence.

lines.text: Over eleven months, teachers reported the drafting fell from up to three hours to about forty five minutes per student.
lines.note: The quietest, most certain line in the first half. Deliver the numbers flat, no lift on the last word, then a full beat.

lines.text: Nationally, a 2025 study found AI drafted plans matched teacher written ones in quality, and still saved time after teachers reviewed them.
lines.note: Measured and informational. Emphasis on 'still saved time'.

lines.text: Not everyone is comfortable. Privacy advocate Amelia Vance warns that the more places information sits, the more places it can be breached from.
lines.intent: Turn to the privacy concern, fairly
lines.note: Drop in energy and slow slightly. Even-handed, no alarm. Short beat after 'comfortable'. Read the name Amelia Vance plainly.

lines.text: She would tell families up front and let them opt out. Mesquite sent no separate notice, saying the tool supports work the district already does.
lines.note: Same level tone for her view and the district's reply, no tilt. Let 'no separate notice' sit as a fact.

lines.text: Panorama says licensed staff still review, revise and finalize every plan. The folder closes before the sun goes down.
lines.intent: Close on the human, a quiet release
lines.note: Settle lower than the middle. Plain on the first sentence, then the last line soft and quietly pleased, a small smile, and let it end without a lift.
